dem_geodetic_slope — DEM geodesy op

• Data kinds: depth → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.dem_geodetic_slope(dem, lat0_deg, d_lat_deg, d_lon_deg, method='horn', units='degrees') (to call the implementation directly, import demops; demops.dem_geodetic_slope(dem, lat0_deg, d_lat_deg, d_lon_deg, method='horn', units='degrees'); from the registry, opsdem.get("dem_geodetic_slope"))

Usage

Slope of a DEM on a latitude-longitude grid (equal angular spacing). The cell dimensions vary with latitude.

Many public DEMs are equally spaced in angle, like a "1-arc-second mesh". Passing this grid as is to dem_slope with a fixed cell size ignores that the real distance in the longitude direction is shorter by a factor of cos(latitude). Using the latitude-direction size for both axes makes east-west slopes too small (half at 60 degrees north), and using the longitude-direction size for both axes makes north-south too large instead. Which way it goes depends on what was taken as constant, so rather than memorising "too large/too small", computing the size per latitude is the right answer.

★ At first this docstring said "east-west becomes too large", but when measured in a test it came out half (too small). Measure claims about sign or direction before writing them.

Here the east-west cell size is computed per latitude, and the grid is converted to equal distances before measuring.

Args:

dem: (H, W). Row 0 is north.

lat0_deg: latitude of the north-west corner [degrees].

d_lat_deg / d_lon_deg: latitude/longitude step per cell [degrees]. Positive values.

method / units: same as dem_slope.
